gate: n/a (CPU-only analysis of GPU measurement logs; no gate run)
method: measure_act_curve.py (from gpu-sim-7uz2) run on the idle RTX 5090 at two contrasting shapes, d_ff/d=4 and batch 1 held fixed so the comparison is about SHAPE not size. Logs are the script's per-rep stdout lines (seq=... rep=... af=...).
caveat: CORRECTED 2026-10-29: an earlier version of this file said neighbour occupancy was NOT recorded for these runs. That was FALSE -- the raw logs carry neighbours_before/after, and the reviewer was right to check. What the logs show: the 4L d2048 run (which produced the LOW extreme at seq 2048) ran with a growing neighbour load -- ~1020 MiB resident before, ~4.0 GB after (1020 + 2418 + 628 MiB) -- while the 16L d512 run ran much lighter (~0.8 GB). So the 48.2% short-sequence spread COINCIDES with differing neighbour occupancy. It is repeatable across 3 reps, which argues against pure transient interference, but occupancy is a confound that has not been excluded. RE-MEASURED ON A QUIET CARD 2026-10-29: values reproduce exactly at matched occupancy, so 48.2% is NOT provisional -- the confound is excluded (see occupancy_confound_resolved); the long-sequence convergence (1.0-1.3%) is measured under similarly mixed occupancy and is the more robust part of the finding.
finding: act_factor is SHAPE-DEPENDENT AT SHORT SEQUENCE and CONVERGES AT LONG SEQUENCE: 48% across shapes at seq 2048, 1.0-1.3% at seq 16384-32768. The single-curve simplification the error budget relies on is therefore VALID WHERE IT IS USED (the deciding cell N16_seq32768) and invalid at short sequences.
mechanism: At long sequence the activation term is dominated by real token activations (scaling with seq x d x layers), so the per-token-per-layer coefficient converges across shapes. At short sequence fixed overheads -- allocator behaviour, fragmentation, workspace -- dominate and are attributed to the coefficient, which is where the apparent shape dependence comes from.
status: MEASUREMENT COMPLETE; anchoring (produced facts, doc sentence, guard + plant) still open on gpu-sim-006j.

occupancy_per_run.implication: the short-sequence spread and occupancy differ together; re-measure short sequences on a quiet card before quoting 48.2% as a hardware property.

occupancy_confound_resolved.conditions: GPU idle window: 0% utilisation, 1342 MiB used, neighbours 16/67/1030 MiB -- and BOTH shapes ran under the SAME ~1030 MiB neighbour, so shapes are compared at matched occupancy for the first time.
occupancy_confound_resolved.result: IDENTICAL to the original runs, to 4 decimal places, at every short sequence length.
occupancy_confound_resolved.conclusion: The 48.2% short-sequence spread is NOT occupancy-driven. The earlier coincidence (4L ran with ~4.0 GB of neighbours, 16L with ~0.8 GB) was exactly that -- a coincidence. The PROVISIONAL marker is therefore LIFTED; the spread is a reproducible property of shape at short sequence, and the mechanism (fixed overheads attributed to the coefficient) stands.
